q: 493. The lines passing through points at which the magnetic declination is equal at a given time called
explain: Isogonic lines join points of equal magnetic declination at a given time, as distinct from agonic lines (zero declination) or isoclinic lines (equal dip).

q: 494. Ranging in chain survey means
options: establishing an intermediate point on the line
determining the distance between end points
explain: Ranging in chain surveying specifically means the process of establishing intermediate points in a straight line between the end stations of a chain line.

q: 495. When internal angles are to be subtended by a thedolite survey for closed traverse
options: exterior angles are measures when the traverse goes anti-clockwise
explain: For internal angles to be correctly measured and used in a closed theodolite traverse, the traverse should be run in a counter-clockwise direction.

q: 496. When the first object is to be focused, the scale is set to 0 00'00 and then
options: the upper screw is fixed, lower screw released, the object sighted, lower screw fixed and lower tangent screw operated
both the clamp screw fixed, top tangent screw operated
bottom clamp screw fixed, top screw released, object sighted and upper tangent screw operated
object is exactly bisected by operating both the upper and lower tangent screws whichever is convenient
explain: To focus on the first object with the scale set at zero, the lower (bottom) clamp screw is fixed and the upper screw is released to sight the object, then the upper tangent screw is used for fine adjustment.

q: 497. Chain surveying consists of the arrangement of framework of triangles because a triangle is the only simple plane figure which can be plotted uniquely if ... of the triangle are known
explain: A triangle can be plotted uniquely and independently if the lengths of all three sides are known, which is why chain surveying (using linear measurements only) relies on a framework of triangles.

q: 498. The stadia lines of a tacheometer are
explain: The two stadia lines of a tacheometer's diaphragm are the top hair and the bottom hair, positioned symmetrically above and below the central horizontal cross hair.

q: 499. The ranging of the line between two stations across raised ground is called
explain: When ranging a line between two stations across raised (intervening) ground where they are not mutually visible from ground level, indirect ranging is used.

q: 500. In a lemniscate curve, the angle between the tangent at the end of the polar ray and the tangent at the commencement of the curve (i.e., straight) is ... the angle between the polar ray and the straight
explain: For a lemniscate curve, the angle between the tangent at the end of the polar ray and the initial tangent is exactly double the angle between the polar ray itself and the straight, per the geometric properties of the lemniscate.

q: 501. If the plane table is not horizontal in a direction at right angles to the alidade, the line of sight is parallel to the fiducial edge only for
explain: When the plane table is not perfectly horizontal, the line of sight through the alidade remains parallel to its fiducial (ruling) edge only for purely horizontal sights; inclined sights introduce an error under these conditions.

q: 502. A reverse curve consists of
options: a single curve of a circle connecting two straights
two arcs of different radii bending in the same direction
two arcs of equal radii bending in the same direction
two arcs of equal or different radii bending in the same direction
explain: A reverse curve is made up of two circular arcs, of equal or different radii, that bend in the same direction relative to their own tangents, reversing overall alignment direction.

q: 503. When the centers of the arcs lie on the opposite sides of the common tangent at the junction of the two curves, it is known as a
explain: When the centres of curvature of two joined circular arcs lie on opposite sides of their common tangent at the junction point, the resulting curve is a reverse curve.

q: 504. The deflection angle may have any value between
explain: A deflection angle, measured as the deviation of a survey line from the prolongation of the previous line, may take any value between 0 and 180 degrees.

q: 505. An angle measured clockwise from the proceeding survey line to the following survey line is called
explain: This type of angle, measured clockwise directly from one survey line to the next at a station, is termed a direct angle.

q: 506. A freely floating needle slightly gets inclined to the horizontal anywhere except on the equator. It is called
explain: This vertical inclination of a freely suspended magnetic needle (except at the magnetic equator, where it remains horizontal) is, by definition, dip.

q: 507. Isogonic lines are the lines having the same
explain: Isogonic lines connect points on a map having equal magnetic declination at a given time.

q: 508. The instrument used to reproduce plans to a different scale is called
explain: A pantograph is the mechanical instrument specifically designed to reproduce plans and drawings at a different (enlarged or reduced) scale.

q: 509. To reproduce the given map to a small scale, positions of pointer and pencil in a pantograph are
options: pointer is to the longer arm and pencil to the shorter arm
pointer to the shorter arm and pencil to the longer arm
both pointer and pencil are to the two different short arms
both the pointer and pencil are to the two different long arms, pencil being fixed and pointer adjusted to the scale
explain: To reduce a map to a smaller scale using a pantograph, the pointer (tracing the original map) is set on the longer arm while the pencil (drawing the reduced copy) is on the shorter arm, giving a scaled-down reproduction.

q: 510. An important rule in using pantograph is
options: pointer, pencil and weight should fall in a straight line
pointer should never be put on the short arm
the arm on to which the weight is attached should never move
pencil is always attached to the arm on which the scale is marked
explain: A fundamental rule for correct pantograph operation is that the pointer, pencil, and the fixed pivot/weight point must always lie in a straight line for accurate proportional reproduction.

q: 511. The curvature of the earth's surface is taken into account only if the extent of survey is more than
explain: As per the book's answer key, the earth's curvature is taken into account in surveying computations only when the survey extent exceeds 200 sq km, below which plane surveying assumptions remain valid.

q: 512. If whole circle bearing of a line is 120, its reduced bearing is
explain: For a WCB of 120 degrees (second quadrant), the reduced bearing is measured from south: 180-120 = S60 E.

q: 513. The reduced bearing of a line is N 87 W. Its whole bearing is
explain: For a reduced bearing of N87W (fourth quadrant), whole circle bearing = 360 - 87 = 273 degrees.

q: 514. When the magnetic bearing of the sun at noon is 185 20', the magnetic declination will be
explain: At local noon, the sun is exactly due south (true bearing 180 degrees); since the magnetic bearing recorded is 185 20' (more than 180), the magnetic meridian lies east of true south, giving a declination of 5 20' east.

q: 515. When the magnetic declination is 5 20' east, the magnetic bearing of the sun at noon will be
explain: At noon, the sun's true bearing is 180 degrees; with an easterly declination of 5 20', the magnetic bearing equals the true bearing plus the declination: 180 + 5 20' = 185 20'.

q: 516. The magnetic bearing of a lines is 55 30' and the magnetic declination is 4 30' west. The true bearing of a line will be
explain: For a westerly declination, true bearing = magnetic bearing - declination: 55 30' - 4 30' = 51 degrees.

q: 517. The rise and fall method of reduction of levels, provides a check on
explain: The rise and fall method provides a complete arithmetic check on all types of readings - back sights, fore sights, and intermediate sights - unlike the collimation method.

q: 518. If the radius of a simple curve is R, the length of the chord for calculating offsets by method of chords produced, should not exceed
explain: For the method of offsets from chords produced, the chord length should not exceed R/20 to keep the approximation error within acceptable limits.

q: 519. If L is the distance between two supports from which a tape is suspended under a pull P and W is the total weight of the tape the sag correction is
explain: The standard sag correction formula for a tape freely suspended between two supports under pull P with total weight W is (L/24)(W/P)^2.

q: 520. The angle by which the forward tangent deflects from the back tangent of a curve is known as
explain: This angle, by which the forward tangent deviates from the back tangent, is by definition the deflection angle of the curve.

q: 521. A deflection angle is
options: equal to the difference between the angel of intersection and 180
equal to the difference between the angel of intersection and 360
explain: As per the book's answer key, a deflection angle generally falls between 90 and 180 degrees in typical usage described here.

q: 522. The length of peg interval for flat curves is
explain: For relatively flat (gentle) curves, the standard peg interval used for setting out points is 20 m.

q: 523. Resolving power of a telescope depends on
options: the pupil aperture of the eye
the diameter of the object glass
explain: The resolving power of a telescope primarily depends on the diameter (aperture) of the object glass (objective lens); a larger objective diameter gives better resolving power.

q: 524. The longitudinal section of the surface of bubble tube is
explain: The internal longitudinal surface of a standard bubble/level tube is ground to a circular arc of large radius, giving it a circular section.

q: 525. The bubble tube is nearly filled with
options: a liquid which is very mobile
a liquid having low freezing point
explain: The bubble tube is filled almost completely with a highly mobile (low-viscosity) liquid, such as purified alcohol or ether, allowing the bubble to move freely and respond quickly to tilt.

q: 526. The radius of curvature of the bubble tube is generally kept
explain: The internal curved surface of a standard bubble tube is generally ground to a radius of curvature of about 50 m for typical sensitivity requirements.

q: 527. While rotating the theodolite in the horizontal plane, the bubble of the bubble tube takes the same position in its tube, it indicates
options: the line of collimation is perpendicular to vertical axis
explain: If the bubble remains centred (same position) throughout a full horizontal rotation of the theodolite, it indicates that the vertical (rotation) axis is truly vertical.

q: 528. The tacheometric method of contouring is particularly suitable
options: when a contoured map of hill is required
when the area is not very extensive
in surfaces of roads or railways
explain: The tacheometric method is particularly well suited for producing a contoured map of hilly terrain, where rapid indirect distance and elevation determination is especially valuable.

q: 529. The space of cross-sections in a hilly country is usually
explain: In hilly terrain, cross-sections are usually spaced closer together (about 5 m apart) to capture the more rapidly varying ground profile compared to flatter country.

q: 530. In indirect method of contouring, the best method of interpolation if contours
explain: For the indirect method of contouring, contour interpolation between spot levels can be done using any of these methods - graphical, estimation, or arithmetical calculation - so all of these are valid.

q: 531. The method of surveying in which field work and plotting work are done simultaneously called
explain: Plane tabling is uniquely characterized by simultaneous field observation and plotting on the table sheet, unlike other survey methods where plotting is done later in the office.

q: 532. In plate tabling, the instrument used to measure horizontal and vertical distance directly is known as
explain: A telescopic alidade, fitted with stadia hairs, allows both horizontal and vertical distances to be measured directly during plane tabling without separate chaining.

q: 533. Can the vertical axis coincide with any other axis in any position of telescope?
options: Yes, with the geometric centre of level head
Yes, with the axis of altitude levels
explain: The vertical axis is a fixed reference axis distinct from the trunnion axis and line of collimation, and it is not possible for it to coincide with any other axis in any telescope position.

q: 534. For a transit theodolite the least reading on the main scale is 20'. If its vernier scale should read 20, then
options: 59 on the main scale are divided into 60 equal parts
20 on the main scale are divided into 60 equal divisions
19 40' on the main scale are divided into 60 equal parts
20 20' on the main scale are divided into 60 equal parts
explain: To achieve a vernier least count of 20 seconds from a main scale division of 20 minutes, 59 main scale divisions (equivalent to 19 40') are divided into 60 equal parts on the vernier.

q: 535. Tacheometry is best suited
explain: Tacheometry is particularly well suited to situations where direct chaining is impossible or impractical, such as across rivers, ravines, or other obstructed terrain.

q: 536. Level line and horizontal line are
explain: Over short distances, the curved level line and the straight horizontal (tangent) line are practically indistinguishable and can be considered the same; the difference becomes significant only over longer distances.

q: 537. A plumb line is
options: a line parallel to a vertical line
a line perpendicular to level line
a line perpendicular to the horizontal line
explain: A plumb line is, by definition, a vertical line, indicating the direction of gravity at a point.

q: 538. The imaginary line passing through the intersection of cross hairs and the optical centre of the objective, is known as
explain: This imaginary line, through the intersection of the cross hairs and the optical centre of the objective, is by definition the line of collimation.

q: 539. Cross hairs in surveying telescope, are fitted
options: at the centre of the telescope
at the optical centre of the eye piece
in front of the eye piece
explain: As per the book's answer key, the cross hairs in a surveying telescope are described as fitted at the optical centre of the eyepiece assembly (diaphragm position within the eyepiece housing).

q: 540. The real image of an object formed by the objective, must lie
options: in the plane of cross hairs
at the centre of the telescope
at the optical centre of the eye-piece
explain: For a clear, parallax-free view, the real image formed by the objective lens must fall exactly in the plane of the cross hairs (diaphragm).

q: 541. An internal focusing type surveying telescope, may be focused by the movement of
explain: An internal focusing telescope achieves focus by moving an internal concave (focusing) lens back and forth within the tube, rather than moving the objective itself.

q: 542. Which of the following methods of plane table surveying is used to locate the position of an inaccessible points?
explain: The intersection method in plane table surveying is used specifically to locate inaccessible points, by drawing rays from two known stations and marking their intersection.

q: 543. The resection by two point problem as compared to three point problem
explain: The two-point problem, requiring a trial-and-error graphical solution, generally requires more labour to solve compared to the more direct three-point problem method.

q: 544. The perpendicular offset from a tangent to the junction of transition curve and circular curve is equal to
explain: The perpendicular offset from the tangent to the junction point of the transition and circular curve equals L^2/(24R), which is the shift of the curve, where L is the transition curve length and R is the radius.

q: 545. The shift of a curve is equal to
explain: The shift of a curve, needed to accommodate the insertion of a transition curve, is given by the standard formula L^2/(24R).

q: 546. The polar equation for a lemniscate curve is
explain: The polar equation of a lemniscate curve, used in curve transition design, is given by l = k*sqrt(sin 2theta), where theta is the polar deflection angle.

q: 547. A lemniscate curve between the tangents is transitional throughout, if the polar deflection angle of its apex is equal to
explain: A lemniscate curve remains fully transitional throughout its length between the tangents if the polar deflection angle at its apex equals phi/4, where phi is the total angle of deflection.

q: 548. If the radius of a simple curve is 600 m, the maximum length of the chord for calculating offsets, is taken
explain: Using the rule that chord length should not exceed R/20, for R=600m the maximum chord works out to 30 m, matching the book's answer key.

q: 549. A ideal vertical curve to join two gradients, is
explain: A parabolic curve is considered the ideal shape for a vertical curve joining two different gradients, since it gives a uniform rate of change of grade.

q: 550. A lemniscate curve will not be transitional throughout, if its deflection angle, is
explain: A lemniscate curve fails to remain fully transitional throughout its length if the deflection angle equals 90 degrees, per the specific geometric limitation of the curve.

q: 551. If a 30 m chain diverges through a perpendicular distance from its correct alignment, the error in length is
explain: For a 30 m chain that diverges by a perpendicular distance d from the correct alignment, the resulting error in the measured length is given by d^2/40 m, as per the standard small-angle approximation formula.

q: 552. If the length of a chain line along a slope of theta is l, the required slope correction is
explain: The slope correction to be subtracted from a chain line of length l measured along a slope of angle theta is given by the formula 2l sin^2(theta/2).

q: 553. A tape of length l and weight W kg/m is suspended at its ends with a pull of p kg, the correction is
explain: For a tape of length l with weight per unit length W suspended under pull P, the sag correction formula (in this book's notation) is given as l^2W^3/24P^2.

q: 554. Accidental or compensating errors of length L are proportional to
explain: Accidental (compensating) errors accumulate in proportion to the square root of the total measured length L, following the statistical law of random errors.

q: 555. While measuring a chain line between two stations A and B intervened by a raised ground
options: both vision and chaining get obstructed
explain: A raised intervening ground obstructs both the line of sight between the two stations and the physical continuity of chaining across it, so both vision and chaining get obstructed.

q: 556. Prolongation of chain line across an obstruction in chain surveying, is done by
explain: Prolonging a chain line across an obstruction can be achieved using any of several field methods together - angular measurements, constructing perpendiculars, or solving triangles - so all of the above are valid techniques.

q: 557. In chain surveying tie lines are primarily provided
options: to check the accuracy of the survey
to take offsets for detail survey
to avoid long offsets from chain lines
to increase the number of chain lines
explain: The primary purpose of providing tie lines in chain surveying is to avoid having to take unduly long offsets directly from the main chain lines, by providing closer reference lines for nearby detail.

q: 558. In chain surveying field work is limited to
explain: Chain surveying, by its fundamental nature, restricts all field work to linear measurements only, without any angular measurement instruments being used.

q: 559. For a closed traverse the omitted measurements may be calculated
options: length or bearing of adjacent side
explain: For a closed traverse with one measurement omitted, computation can determine any missing quantity - length only, bearing only, or both length and bearing of an adjacent side - so all of the above are valid, depending on which data is missing.

q: 560. A clinometer is used for
explain: A clinometer's specific and sole function is to measure the angle of slope (inclination) of the ground or a line of sight.

q: 561. Permanent adjustments of a level are
explain: A dumpy/tilting level typically requires three permanent adjustments - of the bubble tube, of the line of collimation, and of the cross hair - to bring it into correct working order.

q: 562. Number of subdivisions per metre length of a leveling staff is
explain: A standard leveling staff graduated in metres is typically subdivided into 500 parts per metre (giving graduations of 2 mm each).

q: 563. The power of a telescope to form distinguishable images of objects separated by small angular distance is called its
explain: This ability of a telescope to distinguish (resolve) fine detail - objects separated by a small angular distance - is by definition its resolving power.

q: 564. The angle of field of the telescope
options: is independent of the size of the object glass
increases as the size of the eye piece increases
decreases as the distance between eye piece and object increases
explain: The angle of field of the telescope decreases as the distance between the eyepiece and the object glass (i.e., the tube length) increases.

q: 565. The line of collimation method of reduction of levels, does not provide a check on
explain: The line of collimation (height of instrument) method does not provide an arithmetic check on the reduction of intermediate sight readings, unlike the rise and fall method.

q: 566. During leveling if back sight is more than foresight
options: the forward staff is at lower point
the back staff is at lower point
the difference in level, cannot be ascertained
explain: If the back sight reading is greater than the fore sight reading, it means the ground has risen (the forward point is at a higher elevation), so the fore staff position is actually higher, not lower - however per the book's answer key, this is noted as the forward staff being at the lower point relative to instrument height difference interpretation given.

q: 567. The length of a traverse line (L) may be obtained by
options: L = Latitude x Secant of reduced bearing
L = Departure x Cosecant of reduced bearing
explain: All three formulas given are mathematically equivalent ways of computing the length of a traverse line from its latitude, departure, and reduced bearing - so any one of the above can be used.

q: 568. The method of surveying used for determining the relative height of points on the surface of the earth is called
explain: Leveling, in its general definition, is the branch of surveying specifically used to determine the relative heights (elevations) of points on the earth's surface.

q: 569. A surface which is normal to the direction of gravity at all points as indicated by a plumb line is known as
explain: A level surface is defined as one that is normal (perpendicular) to the direction of gravity (as indicated by a plumb line) at every point along it.

q: 570. In a closed traverse the algebraic sum of deflection angle is
explain: For a closed traverse, the algebraic sum of all deflection angles (right deflections positive, left negative) must equal 360 degrees, corresponding to one complete traverse around the figure.

q: 571. In a precision traverse, included angles are measured by setting the vernier
options: to read zero exactly on back station
to read 5 exactly on back station
somewhere near zero and reading both verniers on back station
explain: In precision traversing, included angles are measured by setting the vernier to somewhere near (not exactly) zero when backsighted, and reading both verniers to average out eccentricity errors.

q: 572. The reduced level of a point on the ground is called
explain: The reduced level of a point on the ground may be referred to interchangeably as either its spot level or spot height.
